blocks.content:
The President can remove the Chairman or a member on the following grounds:
• Misbehavior (after Supreme Court inquiry)
• Insolvency
• Engaging in paid employment outside official duties
• Infirmity of mind or body
• Conflict of financial interest
The President can remove the Chairman or a member on the following grounds:

items: Crucial distinction: Supreme Court inquiry is mandatory ONLY for removal on grounds of 'Misbehavior'.
Engaging in paid employment outside official duties is a direct ground for President-led removal.
Note that the removal authority is the President, not Parliament.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The President has the power to remove the Chairman or a member from office.
Removal on the specific ground of misbehavior requires an inquiry by the Supreme Court.
Other grounds for removal include insolvency, outside paid employment, infirmity of mind or body, and conflict of financial interest.
